title: Avgolemono Chicken Cutlets and Rice
description: Egg yolk, a little lemon and fresh dill turn the poaching broth into a velvety Greek-style sauce that settles into the rice.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breast
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Plain, unsalted and either freshly cooked or promptly chilled.

steps.title: Even the cutlets
steps.text: Butterfly {chicken} into cutlets. Between two sheets of parchment, gently tap the thick ends with the flat face of a meat mallet to an even 3/8 inch.

steps.title: Warm the rice
steps.text: Put {rice} in the saucepan with a splash of {broth}. Cover over low heat for 4–7 minutes, stirring once, until steaming hot and 165°F throughout. Keep covered.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.text: Heat the remaining broth in the HexClad to a bare simmer. Submerge the cutlets and cover. Poach for 4–8 minutes, turning once until each thickest center reaches 165°F. Hold covered in a little broth.

steps.title: Prepare the egg base
steps.text: Whisk {yolk} with {lemon} in a heatproof bowl until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the poaching broth
steps.text: Boil the poaching broth for 1 minute. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and simmer for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Temper the yolk
steps.text: Gradually whisk several spoonfuls of hot thickened broth into the yolk mixture until warm and fluid.

steps.title: Finish the lemon sauce
steps.text: Whisk the tempered yolk into the skillet over low heat. Stir constantly for 1–3 minutes, until the sauce reaches 160°F and flows evenly off the spoon. Take off heat and stir in {dill}.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Divide the hot rice between two bowls. Thinly slice the cutlets and lay them on the rice, then ladle the warm lemon sauce generously over both.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups of sauce for two, in addition to the rice. Make ahead: Use promptly chilled rice from the previous day or cook it fresh. Make the egg sauce just before serving. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The egg-enriched sauce can separate after freezing. For freezer prep, freeze the chicken in its plain thickened broth for up to 2 months and add fresh yolk and lemon after reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm the rice and chicken in the sauce over low heat, covered, stirring often and adding a splash of water if needed. Check from 6 minutes until rice, chicken and sauce reach 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses the measured lemon juice. For gentler Option B, start with a few drops in the yolk and add more dill. The sauce contains no dairy. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 298 kcal, 36.5 g protein, 21.1 g total carbohydrate, 6.1 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 98 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth.
